svg.title: CELL Preservation technology — CPLL / EGCG platform schematic (v6, English)
svg.desc: Schematic illustration in three parts. i Preservation concept: cell protection, preservation flexibility (frozen and non-frozen) and functional recovery — cell-friendly preservation. ii Core technologies, shown as two distinct technologies. CPLL (carboxylated poly-L-lysine, an antifreeze polyamino acid) for cryopreservation by slow freezing and vitrification: proposed mechanism of interaction near the cell membrane, suppression of ice crystal growth and of ice recrystallization (shown separately); leads to DMSO-free formulation options. EGCG (green tea polyphenol) for non-frozen preservation: under evaluated non-cytotoxic conditions, EGCG treatment transiently increases the proportion of cells in G0/G1 while progression continues; after removal, cell cycle progression and proliferation recover; antioxidant activity is a separate action. iii Applications (representative examples): stem and various cells and reproductive cells — CPLL; tissues such as cornea and cartilage — EGCG; organoids — CPLL, research and development; cell sheets (chondrocyte and myoblast sheets) — CPLL, vitrification research. Not to scale.

g.text: Designed to reduce the burden on cells
Two core technologies with distinct actions
May help reduce freezing stress on cells (schematic)
Enabling the design of DMSO-free formulations
A separate action from cell cycle regulation
